texts.preamble: Ajay Kumar vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2024 Criminal Appeal no. 42/17 Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector In The Court Of Sh. Devender Kumar Jangala Asj-05, Patiala House Court, New Delhi District, New Delhi Dlnd010023002017 Criminal Appeal no. 42/17 Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector 26.04.2024 Ajay Kumar S/o Sh. Nathuni, Masala Stall, Pilli Kothi Chowk Bijli Road, Naya Bazar, Delhi-110006 ......... Appellant Versus Food Inspector Directorate of Pfa Government of Nct of Delhi A-20, Lawrence Road Industrial Area Delhi-110035 .....Respondent Date of institution : 19.04.2017 Date of arguments : 16.04.2024 Date of order : 26.04.2024 Appearances: Sh. G. P. Saxena, Sh. R. P. Pandey and Ms. Ishani, Advocates on behalf of appellant. Sh.Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor for respondent/Department. J U D G M E N T:
texts.facts: 3. Brief facts: It is alleged that on 19.04.2011, Food Inspector S. B. Singh purchased a sample of Kali Mirch from the appellant Ajay Kumar under the supervision of Local Health Authority(LHA)/SDM for analysis. The said sample was sent to the Public Analysist who declared the alleged sample adulterated because it found containing 'mineral oil' and did not confirm to the standard because 'light berries' exceeds beyond the prescribed limit. On the basis of report of Public Analysist complaint dated 28.06.2011 was filed by Food Inspector. The appellant in exercise of his right under Section 13(2) of PFA get the sample analyzed by the central laboratory who also declared the sample adulterated because of presence of 'mineral oil' etc in the sampled article. Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector 4. The Ld. Trial Court after framing of notice proceeded for trial and recorded the statement of prosecution witnesses. The appellant/convict being aggrieved by the order of conviction and order on the point of sentence has filed the present appeal. It is argued that the judgment of Ld.Trial Court is based on prediction and assumptions and suffers from errors of law and appreciation of evidence. That the sanctioning authority has given the sanction to file the present case against the appellant without application of his mind and without going through the facts of the case. 6. Notice of the present appeal was issued to the respondent/department. The respondent/department put appearance being represented by Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor and strongly opposed the appeal filed by the appellant.
texts.arguments: It is submitted that none of the grounds of appeal are sustainable in the eyes of law. 8. In the present appeal it is contended that that the Ld. Trial Court has fails to appreciate that the witnesses deposed before the court were against the facts and contradictory to each other. 9. It is also argued that the sanctioning authority has given the sanction without application of mind. 10. It is also contended that the Ld. Trial Court has fails to appreciate that the reports of both the laboratories were divergent, vague and fictitious. 12. It is submitted by Ld.counsel for the appellant/convict that in the present matter the PA report or the CFL report has fails to distinguish whether the mineral oil found in the sample was food grade or not. Ld.counsel for the accused has relied upon one judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court reported as 2007(2) JCC 1154 State Vs. Dwarka Dass wherein Hon'ble High Court was pleased to held: "The report of Public Analyst standards superseded by the report of Director, CFL. On this issue, I have relied upon one latest judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as M/s A. K. Ajay Kumar Vs. Food Inspector Sarkar & Company & Anr. Vs. The State of West Bengal & Ors, Special Leave Petition(Criminal) No.6095 of 2018, dated 07.03.2024, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has observed that: "Whether the appellant can be granted the benefit of the new legislation and be awarded a lesser punishment as is presently prescribed under the new law. This court in T. Barai VS. Henry Ah Hoe (1983) 1 SCC 177, had held that when an amendment is beneficial to the accused it can be applied even to cases pending the courts where Ajay Kumar vs Food Inspector on 26 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40683698/ 5 such a provision did not exist at the time of commission of offence." 19. The recent judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr.(supra) has made it clear that if there is an amendment in the Act, which is beneficial to the accused, it can be applied even to the pending cases in the court where such provision was not in existence. The ratio of judgment M/s A. K. Sarkar & Company & Anr.(supra) is squarely applicable to the facts of present case.
